frequency_question: How often do structural and operational frictions successfully prevent targeted scaling of debt management or liquidity interventions?
membership_rule: Includes announced programs intended to scale up purchase or intervention volumes significantly over a defined multi-year horizon; excludes ad-hoc emergency interventions of short duration.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Large-Scale Asset Purchases (QE1 scaling, 2009)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major programmatic scaling efforts identified and examined; all achieved target operational volumes.
known_gaps: Sample size is small because large-scale structural buyback and liquidity programs initiated by the U.S. Treasury and Federal Reserve are rare historical events.
skeleton: 5 distinct liquidity/debt management scaling initiatives since 2000, each successfully reaching desired operational volume targets despite structural frictions.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 5 applicable historical program scaling instances.
validity_reason: Institutional operational capacity and primary dealer mechanics evolve slowly over multi-decade periods.
